The appellants instituted Title Suit No. 22 of 1976 subsequently renumbered as Title Suit I No,42 of 1982 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Jhenidah against the defendant-respondents i praying for selling aside the ex parte decree dated 27.8.1974 which they obtained in their Title Suit No. 3 of 1959 on the allegations, inter alia, that the respondents instituted Title Suit No. 82 of 1956 in the Second Court of Munsif at Jhenidah for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession of the suit land measuring 16 acres from the : appellants but the plaint of that suit having been returned they filed Title Suit No. 3 of 1959 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Jhenidah. That suit was dismissed but on appeal by the respondents being Title Appeal No. 158 of 1964 the appellate Court allowed the appeal and sent the suit on remand to the trial Court and thereafter the learned (Subordinate Judge decreed the suit ex parte on 27.8.1974. The respondents put the ex parte decree into execution in Title Execution Case No. 9 of 1974 and got delivery of possession of the suit land on 22.9.1974. The appellants coming to know about the ex parte decree instituted Title Suit (No. 224 of 1976 in the Court of the Subordinate r Judge, Jessore which was transferred to the Court of Subordinate Judge, Jhenidah and registered there as Title Suit No. 224 of 1976 which was ultimately renumbered as Title Suit No.42 of 1982, praying for setting aside the ex parte decree dated 27.8.1974 passed in Title Suit No. 3 of 1959. 

 7. In the instant case the appellants succeeded both in the trial Court as well as in the appellate Court in setting aside the ex parte decree obtained by the respondents. There is no doubt the respondents have preferred a revision case before the High Court Division. Simply because the property in suit was under the management of a receiver for a long period of time it cannot be regarded as a just and convenient ground for appointment of a receiver as Order XL rule (I) does not authorise Court to do so on such a ground. Further, the respondents instituted their suit in 1956 for declaration of their title and recovery of khas possession of the property and till 22.11.1974 the appellants were in possession of the suit property and there was no receiver nor the respondents ever prayed for appointment of a receiver for a period of about 18 years till the suit was decreed ex parte on 27.8.1974. In the facts and circumstances of the case the order of appointment of a receiver of the property in suit by the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division cannot be considered to be an order passed in proper exercise of discretion and, as such, it is liable to be set aside.
